questions.question_text: A circle has a radius of $8\text{ cm}$. What is the exact area of a sector with central angle $\dfrac{\pi}{4}\text{ radians}$?

options.why: Forgot the factor of $\frac{1}{2}$ in the sector area formula.
Did not square the radius ($A = \frac{1}{2}r\theta$, calculating arc length instead).
Calculated the area of the entire circle $\pi r^2$.

questions.question_text: A sector of a circle of radius $6\text{ cm}$ subtends an angle of $45^{\circ}$ at the centre. Find the exact area of the sector.

options.why: Substituted degrees directly into $A = \frac{1}{2}r^2\theta$ without converting to radians.
Used $90^{\circ}$ instead of $45^{\circ}$ or forgot the factor of $\frac{1}{2}$.
Omitted $\pi$ when converting degrees to radians.

questions.question_text: A sector has a radius of $10\text{ cm}$ and an arc length of $7\text{ cm}$. What is the area of the sector?

options.why: Multiplied radius by arc length without the factor of $\frac{1}{2}$.
Appended $\pi$ unnecessarily to the decimal area value.
Halved both the radius and arc length before multiplying.

questions.question_text: A circular sector has an area of $20\pi\text{ cm}^{2}$ and a central angle of $\dfrac{2\pi}{5}\text{ radians}$. What is the radius of the circle?

options.why: Found $r^2$ but forgot to take the square root.
Forgot the factor of $\frac{1}{2}$ when rearranging, leading to $r^2 = 25$.
Carried $\pi$ into the linear radius measurement.

questions.question_text: A sector of a circle of radius $6\text{ cm}$ has an area of $12\text{ cm}^{2}$. What is the central angle $\theta$ in radians?

options.why: Divided area by $r^2$ instead of $\frac{1}{2}r^2$ (forgot the factor of $\frac{1}{2}$).
Inverted the quotient when solving for angle ($r^2 \div 2A$).
Divided $12$ by $6$ directly without squaring the radius.

questions.question_text: A minor sector in a circle of radius $6\text{ cm}$ has a central angle of $\dfrac{\pi}{6}\text{ radians}$. Find the exact area of the major sector.

options.why: Calculated the minor sector area instead of the major sector area.
Calculated the total circle area.
Subtracted from $\pi$ instead of $2\pi$ when finding the major angle.

questions.question_text: A circular cake of radius $15\text{ cm}$ is sliced into $8$ equal sectors. What is the exact area of one slice?

options.why: Divided full circle area by $4$ instead of $8$.
Did not square the radius ($15$ instead of $15^2$).
Omitted $\pi$ from the exact calculation.

questions.question_text: A sector has an area of $A = \dfrac{27\pi}{2}\text{ cm}^{2}$ and a central angle of $\theta = \dfrac{3\pi}{4}\text{ radians}$. What is the radius $r$?

options.why: Forgot to take the square root of $r^2 = 36$.
Forgot the factor of $\frac{1}{2}$ in the sector area formula.
Divided $36$ by $2$ instead of taking the square root.

questions.question_text: The ratio of the area of a minor sector to the area of the remaining major sector is $1:5$. If the radius is $6\text{ cm}$, what is the exact area of the minor sector?

options.why: Divided the total circle area by $5$ instead of $6$ ($1+5$ parts).
Calculated the major sector area instead of the minor sector area.
Divided by $3$ instead of $6$.

questions.solution_text:
The minor sector represents $\dfrac{1}{1+5} = \dfrac{1}{6}$ of the full circle.
$A_{\text{circle}} = \pi(6^{2}) = 36\pi$
$A_{\text{minor}} = \dfrac{1}{6} \times 36\pi = 6\pi\text{ cm}^{2}$
